purpose: A small reviewed question-and-solution supplement for later native live learning; not a replacement for a large reading corpus.
attribution: Selected worked examples adapted from Prealgebra 2e by Lynn Marecek, MaryAnne Anthony-Smith, Andrea Honeycutt Mathis, OpenStax at Rice University, and the contributors credited in the source preface. Source: https://github.com/openstax/osbooks-prealgebra-bundle/tree/bba5f5244066884797f730149d918e33f2beefd1 . This pinned edition declares Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . Changes: selected image-free worked examples extracted from CNXML; MathML serialized to text notation; whitespace and local table labels normalized. No endorsement is implied. The repository MIT license applies to code, not these source passages. Selection changes: individually reviewed complete pairs retained unchanged or omitted in full; whole chapters reserved for evaluation; any overlapping lesson would be omitted in full; none were found by the declared exact checks. The full book is not admitted.
split_policy: Whole Properties of Real Numbers chapter is validation; whole Polynomials chapter is reserved test. All selected examples from each remaining chapter are training. Previously protected text is reserved first, then new test, validation and training. Exact matching of a whole normalized lesson, a normalized question, or a normalized paragraph of at least 120 characters omits the entire later lesson. Authored held-out probe contexts are also protected. No individual question or answer paragraph is removed.

limitations: Every extracted candidate was reviewed by the assistant; no independent expert certification.
This is a small supplement with formula markup, not millions of new examples or proof of QA ability.
Entire chapters are held out, so evaluation measures topic transfer as well as prediction; no claim of an IID split.
Exact overlap checks preserve symbols but do not detect paraphrases, near-duplicates, changed-number templates, or all shared mathematical concepts.
The 2024 source license and original preface are retained; repository MIT terms apply to code.
No native model has learned this edition, and preparation creates no curriculum schedule or teacher/reproduction admission.
